history.period: 1764 CE (built by Swargadeo Rajeswar Singha, r. 1751-1769)
history.summary: CSV DUPLICATE FLAG: this row ('Basistha Temple', Dispur) is almost certainly the same temple as CSV row 82 ('Basistha Temple', Guwahati) - no separate Basistha temple is documented anywhere at Dispur, and the only Basistha Temple on record stands in the Basistha/Beltola area of Guwahati. It is a Shiva temple in the Basisthashram, believed to be the home of sage Vasistha; the existing octagonal brick temple (Nilachal architecture) was built by Ahom king Rajeswar Singha in 1764 over the remains of a stone temple dated ~1000-1100 CE. The garbhagriha is sunken and said to hold the sage's foot impression; the temple stands on the bank of the mountain streams that become the Basistha and Bharalu rivers. Keep one row or merge with seq 82.
history.name: Basistha Temple
history.town: Guwahati - Basistha area (CSV town 'Dispur' is a duplicate row of seq 82; the temple is not in Dispur)
history.town_description: Guwahati is the largest city of Assam and the main gateway to Northeast India, set on the banks of the Brahmaputra river. It is one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in India (ancient Pragjyotishpura) and hosts several major temples including Kamakhya, Navagraha and Umananda.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport - about 25 km west of the temple (verify).
travel.railway: Guwahati Junction railway station - about 14 km (per travel guides; verify).
travel.road: About 10-14 km south-east of the city centre on the Beltola-Basistha road; city buses stop at 'Basistha Mandir'; taxis/autos from anywhere in Guwahati.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant and dry); the mountain streams and waterfall are at their best just after the monsoon.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Widely reported as 7:00 AM-9:00 PM (verify). Modest dress, remove footwear; the meditation cave is ~5 km inside the ashram.
